chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his brother Isḥāq ibn Ibrahim, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Bazīʿ, from al-Riḍā (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'It has reached me that the day of Friday is the shortest of the days.' He said, 'It is so.' I said, 'May I be your ransom, how is that?' He said, 'Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, gathers the souls of the polytheists beneath the eye of the sun. So when the sun stagnates, Allah punishes the souls of the polytheists by the stagnation of the sun for an hour. So when it is the day of Friday, the sun does not stagnate; Allah raises the punishment from them due to the merit of the day of Friday, so the stagnation does not occur for the sun.'
ai.seo_question: Why is Friday considered the shortest day according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: Imam al-Riḍā (peace be upon him) elucidates that Friday is the 'shortest' day because the punishment of polytheist souls in the intermediate realm is suspended for an hour due to the sun's lack of stagnation, a privilege granted by the merit of the day. This narration, found in al-Kulayni’s *al-Kafi*, highlights the unique spiritual status of Friday in Shia eschatology and cosmology, linking celestial mechanics with divine mercy. The concept of 'rukud' (stagnation) serves as a metaphor for the cessation of torment, emphasizing Friday's role as a day of relief and elevation in the cosmic order.
